result.title: Mitigating Overgeneralization in RND via Spectral Target Design
result.summary: Random Network Distillation (RND) is a scalable novelty signal for RL based on a fixed random target network and a trained predictor. However, it can overgeneralize: the predictor extrapolates the random target off the data manifold, causing novelty scores to collapse on unfamiliar inputs. This paper analyzes this failure through a kernel-theoretic lens. Under a GP target model and an NTK-regime predictor, we show that the RND novelty score is a cross-kernel residual variance: it is governed jointly by the target covariance kernel and the predictor NTK, rather than by either one alone. This identifies overgeneralization as spectral under-excitation. Motivated by this view, we formulate spectral target design as a principle for shaping RND novelty geometry. As a concrete instance, we replace the implicit random-network target with a bandwidth-controlled Random Fourier Feature (RFF) target, redistributing residual signal toward modes less attenuated by the predictor. Experiments on offline D4RL, online Atari, and Fetch manipulation benchmarks show improved novelty discrimination and downstream RL performance. The code for the RL implementation is available at https://github.com/tuuktuc86/RFF-RND.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从核理论角度分析 RND 新颖性信号在数据流形外出现的过泛化坍塌，指出其本质是目标协方差核与预测器 NTK 共同决定的谱欠激发，并提出带宽可控的 RFF 目标来重塑新颖性几何。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「残差信号被预测器谱衰减而失效」的分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 表示坍缩、以及 LOOK 阶段判断视觉证据是否足够新颖/不确定提供概念工具，但领域相距较远，需核查可迁移性。
